question: For $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&-2\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$B=\begin{bmatrix}-1&2&0\\3&-1&5\end{bmatrix},$$ evaluate the two matrix expressions $2(A+B)-3A$ and $2B-A$ and use the result to verify the relevant distributive properties of scalar multiplication.
explanation:
Evaluation of the First Expression

Using scalar multiplication over matrix addition, $$2(A+B)=2A+2B$$ Therefore, $$2(A+B)-3A=2A+2B-3A=2B-A$$ We now verify this numerically. First, $$A+B=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&-2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1&2&0\\3&-1&5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&3\\3&3&3\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$2(A+B)=\begin{bmatrix}2&2&6\\6&6&6\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$3A=\begin{bmatrix}6&-3&9\\0&12&-6\end{bmatrix}$$ Thus, $$2(A+B)-3A=\begin{bmatrix}-4&5&-3\\6&-6&12\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification

Also, $$2B=\begin{bmatrix}-2&4&0\\6&-2&10\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$2B-A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&4&0\\6&-2&10\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&-2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-4&5&-3\\6&-6&12\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$2(A+B)-3A=2B-A$$ The equality follows from the distributive properties of scalar multiplication and is verified for the given matrices.
